title: Nitrous oxide anesthesia and plasma homocysteine in adolescents
authors: Nagele P, Tallchief D, Blood J, Sharma A, Kharasch ED
population: Patients aged 10 to 18 years undergoing elective major spine surgery
funder: This research was funded by National Institutes of Health grant number NIH K23GM087534; K24DA00417; UL1RR024992.
authorConflicts: P. Nagele received research funding from Roche Diagnostics; the other authors reported no conflicts of interest.
result: Nitrous oxide inactivates vitamin B12 and inhibits methionine synthase. 26 of 27 patients received nitrous oxide. Plasma total homocysteine rose in all 26 by a geometric mean of 9.4 umol/L (95% CI 7.1 to 12.5), a mean 228%, from a median baseline of 5.1 umol/L; it peaked 6 to 8 hours after induction and largely returned to baseline by 24 hours; the rise correlated with the product of duration and average concentration of nitrous oxide (r = 0.80). The one patient without nitrous oxide had no increase.
